page: Amazon Web Services c7gn.large is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and custom AWS Graviton processors. It features 2 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 architecture, utilizing the ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 model running at 2.6 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, with no hyperthreading support. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It contains no local storage or GPU hardware, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark results show average single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1532.89 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1514.0. However, multi-core and multi-threaded performance is weak to poor, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 3043.47 and a bzip3 multi-threaded decompression speed of 17.68 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth tests show an average read-only large block speed of 57.94 GB/sec, but a weak write speed of 20.86 GB/sec. Cryptographic and complex instruction performance is poor, with a Passmark CPU encryption score of 274.06 and an extended instructions score of 1941.65.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c7gn.large offers dedicated ARM-based compute resources with a low memory footprint, making it a budget-conscious option for workloads that do not require x86 instruction sets or high memory density. Given its 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and average single-threaded performance, the instance is suitable for lightweight network-optimized tasks, basic web serving, and single-threaded utility scripts. It is less suitable for multi-threaded database operations, heavy image processing, or large language model inference due to its weak multi-core and memory benchmark scores.
